title: The Self is ever-present
sum: What is sought is not somewhere else or later. It is already here, only forgotten or covered over. The books keep turning the reader from searching outward to the one who is already present.

ram.t: The Self as being, consciousness, bliss: never absent in past, present or future, waking, dream or sleep.
Attaining what is already attained: always present, forgotten through ignorance.
Self-evident, known by itself and not by another.
"It already is the supreme Self": no one goes anywhere to become it.

chhinna.t: The jiva is always free by nature; its own is the Atma.
"You are already established in samadhi", and how faith in this arises.
"You know your own self; that is why you know everything."

bhagavat.t: Truth is what cannot be negated in the three times, and is self-evident.
"The attainment of the already attained" (praptasya prapti).
"You are never separated from me, the Self of all."
"I stand already where I must go": worship as supposing oneself something.

paigam.t: "I am already everyone's Self: what need is there to do?"
Prisoners of love, always free of both world and doomsday.
Those imprisoned in love, always free.

title: The separate "I" as the veil
sum: The sense of being a separate someone (doer, enjoyer, knower) is what covers the Self. The veil, the curtain, ego and yogamaya are different images for this one covering, and it falls away on knowing "I" as "I".

ram.t: A curtain falls over "I": assumptions cover the Self.
Seeking the Lord by regarding "I" as something, against knowing "I" as "I".
Veiled by yogamaya: knowing "I am a man, a woman, a jiva" is not knowing fully.
Mind arises whenever we regard ourselves as a doer, enjoyer or knower.

chhinna.t: The ego "I am the doer and enjoyer" is itself the bondage of actions.
Awareness of "I-ness" and the one "I".
Doing everything without ego is the nature of doing nothing.

bhagavat.t: Pure knowledge and the veil of yogamaya (Gita 7:25).
The curtain of yogamaya torn off; the veiled one sees all.
"What is this play of the veiled one, as I saw when I lifted the veil?"
"O veiled one, lift the veil!"
"The ego was lost, the lost one was found."

paigam.t: The veil of mind and of Maya, and no veil on the "I".
Without a veil, He sits veiled: let the notion of the veil go.
Ecstasy of selflessness comes when ego (khudi) departs.
Giving up ego in exchange for selfless bliss.
"Lift the veil and see."

title: Grace of the guru
sum: Realisation is not produced by effort alone. It comes through the grace of the guru, the saint, the Lord, and through satsang. In the poems the same grace is the cupbearer, the tavern and the faqir's gaze.

ram.t: The Lord as ocean of grace; his grace is never exhausted.
The Lord's grace is eternal, endless and all-pervading.
Devotion "I am" is born only of grace, received by the grace of the guru.
Without satsang, the company of saints, the state of the Self is hard to attain.
The guru's love for Bharat and Rama's response.

chhinna.t: Practice is for attaining Him by whose grace God is found; who is fit for guru-darshan.
"The grace of the saint is the means."
Inquiry into the Self is itself the grace of Ram.
Introduction, with the banyan-tree verse: the young guru, the old disciples.

bhagavat.t: The four graces: of God, of true scripture, of the Self and of the guru.
Devotion found only through satsang and favourable saints.
Devotion comes by the grace of great souls and of God (Narad Bhakti Sutra).
Aarti to the Sadguru.

paigam.t: "May the faqirs bestow their grace" (poem 6).
"Blessed be your cupbearer" (poem 27).
The tavern and the cupbearer (poem 31).
If the cupbearer is found, everywhere is the tavern.
Getting free or getting caught depends on the dervishes' grace.

title: Name (naam) and remembrance
sum: Ram Darshan gives the Name its fullest treatment. The other books mostly handle it more briefly, as remembrance, as a label for what is only appearance, or as the One Naam.

ram.t: Valmiki and the power of the Name.
Kinds of chanting, including the whispered chant.
"That is no Name and no chant by which the Named is not found."
The glory of the Name for Shankar, Shukdev, Sanak and others.
Remembering the Name ends the cycle of coming and going.

chhinna.t: Name and form: who sees them (Q 86).
The body as the name of what is not (Q 554).
The name "sthitapragya" and where one lives (Q 445).

bhagavat.t: Chant without break the name of God you have faith in.
Japa and remembrance of the name as apara bhakti, resting on feeling.
Japa, tapas and the rest do not make the mind still.
Who gave God the name Bhagavan: the devotees did.
Names as mere labels (Chhandogya 6/1/5).

paigam.t: "The speech of the One Naam" in which Mukta found ecstasy.
Whatever road one takes, one becomes the name that goes with it.

title: One Reality behind names and forms
sum: Pots are clay, ornaments are gold, waves are water. The many names and forms have no existence apart from the one Reality, and seeing a second is the trouble.

ram.t: Speech and meaning, water and waves: called different, yet not different.
In knowing water, the wave has no existence; likewise for "I" and the river.
Five parts of everything: asti, bhati, priya, name and form.
Look at a flower as an infant does: being, appearing, dearness, name and form.
The gold example (a gold image and its gold mount).

chhinna.t: Name and form seen by the one beyond name and form (Q 86).
"There is no second; so whom would it see?" (Q 142).
The proof that "one" has no second (Q 320).
Apart from one there is no second thing (Q 703).

bhagavat.t: Gold and ornament: the final teaching, explained simply.
"Is there an ornament without you, the gold?"
One lump of clay: all clay things are clay alone (Chhandogya).
One piece of iron (Chhandogya).
Rivers abandon name and form in the ocean (Mundaka).
Wave and water.

paigam.t: All names and forms are the shadow of the Self; no second, not even a drop.
The same teaching in a nearby poem.
When there is nothing but the Self, where is enmity or friendship?
"I am that in which it is made and unmade; all the rest are surges."
Bubble-lovers forming and dissolving on the shoreless ocean.

title: Mind as the place of bondage and freedom
sum: Bondage and liberation are said to live in the mind, and the mind itself is called a heap of supposition. The books ask for the mind's existence to be seen through, not controlled.

ram.t: Absence of mind is absence of the world; restlessness itself is mind.
Mind is not controlled by practice.
The senses are one mind, named by their function.
Bondage and liberation listed among the identities to abandon.
Everything seen, heard and pondered is in the mind alone.

chhinna.t: Mind in doing; the Self as no-mind (Q 608 to 614).
No-mind through no-mind (Q 67).
The existence of the mind is to be renounced (Q 717).
Practice to make the mind mindless, not to kill it (Q 832).

bhagavat.t: Bondage and liberation are two names from ignorance.
What a purified mind is; the mind as the heap of vasanas.
When suppositions are absent, the mind is no more.
The mind under control or helpless?
Rivers reaching the ocean and the jiva settling in Hari.

paigam.t: "This mind is my shadow, not separate from me."
Bondage and freedom are tales: lost both alike.
The veil of the mind.
The glossary: dilkashi, the heart dying into no-mind.

title: Living Vedanta
sum: The phrase "living Vedanta" (Vedanta with direct experience) is used for Maharshi Mukt's teaching: knowledge tested in experience and lived in the world, not a theory.

ram.t: "Living Vedanta, Vedanta with direct experience", the name Karpatri gave his teaching.
"Now enter the realm of direct experience."
"Now experience Rama."
"I am not the body": names belong to practical dealings in the world.

chhinna.t: Pure spirituality, or "living Vedanta" (zinda Vedanta), free of sect.
How to live in the world: like a boat in a river (Q 179 to 180).

bhagavat.t: Closing note: Karpatri's "living Vedanta" and Maharshi Mukt.
Direct realization of the Self: Hamsa, the sages Sanaka and others, and Uddhava.
Shukadeva brings Parikshit to direct experience, with the gold teaching.

paigam.t: The world and bliss: being in the world without being bound.
Selflessness in the world; even silence is silent.
"Free the shore, free the boat and boatman."
